fields.description:
## Symptom

Five tests in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py` fail locally for any
developer whose git config sets `safe.bareRepository = explicit`. They pass under git's default
(`all`), which is what CI uses, so **CI can never exercise this path**.

Failing: `test_relevant_remote_rejection_never_places_candidate_on_shared_head`,
`test_successful_push_followed_by_remote_rewrite_fails_closed`,
`test_unrelated_remote_rejection_merges_and_rebuilds_private_candidate`,
`test_lost_push_ack_is_confirmed_without_publishing_a_second_bundle`,
`test_post_push_convergence_preserves_concurrent_local_delivery_pending`.

All five fail identically — not an assertion, a `CalledProcessError` from the test helper:

```
subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['git', '-C',
 '.../tickets-remote.git', 'ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only',
 'refs/heads/tickets', '5c21-6a58-bfa5-4202']' returned non-zero exit status 128
```

## Root cause

`git` refuses to **discover** a bare repository via `-C` / cwd when `safe.bareRepository=explicit`;
it accepts one named by a top-level `--git-dir`. Exit 128 is a refusal to open the repository at
all, *before* any ref lookup:

```
git -C <bare>  -> fatal: cannot use bare repository '<bare>' (safe.bareRepository is 'explicit')
git --git-dir <bare>  -> exit 0
```

The offending helper is `_git` at `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py:40-46`,
which hardcodes `["git", "-C", str(repo), *args]`. The bare remote is built in `_ticket_remote`
(:97-117) and read at **:401, :402, :415, :423, :435** — exactly the five failing tests, one site each.

## Two claims in the original report are wrong and should not be carried forward

1. **"refs/heads/tickets does not exist" is wrong.** The ref exists and resolves fine; git never gets
   as far as looking it up.
2. **"git 2.55.0" is a red herring.** `safe.bareRepository` was introduced in **git 2.38.0
   (2022-10-03)** with exactly these semantics. This behavior has been stable for about four years,
   so there is no version dependency to chase.

## This is a recurrence of a class already fixed, not a new environmental quirk

Closed ticket `3476-4472-3407-4246` (`embolismic-adverse-dragon`), "Bare-repository fixtures fail
under safe.bareRepository=explicit", records the governing policy verbatim:

> "Linux CI currently uses Git defaults and therefore does not expose the failure, but the supported
> test suite must run both locally and in CI. **Treat agents dismissing reproducible local test
> failures as environmental noise as an anti-pattern.**"

That ticket converted 13 files from `git -C <bare>` to `git --git-dir <bare>` and added a held-out
oracle, `tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py`, which runs fixtures
under a strict `safe.bareRepository=explicit` config.

**Why this file escaped the guard:** that oracle pins a **hardcoded allowlist** of fixture nodes
(`_FIXTURE_NODES`, 3 entries). `test_atomic_completion_close.py` was added on 2026-08-25 by commit
`1cb1cdd25aff` — four days *after* the guard landed and three days *before* 3476 closed — and
reintroduced the banned construct at five sites. There is no static sweep either: nothing under
`scripts/`, the `Makefile`, or `.pre-commit-config.yaml` checks for it
(`scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` covers an unrelated concern).

So the guard does not fail when a new file reintroduces the defect; it only checks three files that
were already fixed. **That allowlist is the reason this is the second occurrence, and leaving it is
the reason there would be a third.**

## Measurements

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| target file, default git config, isolated | 17 passed |
| whole `tests/interfaces/lifecycle` directory, default config | 546 passed, exit 0 |
| target file with `safe.bareRepository=explicit` | **5 failed, 12 passed** |

No test pollution and no ordering dependency — the pass/fail split is governed entirely by that one
config value. Reproduced with an ordinary user git config file (no `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` injection), so
it is not a harness artifact: `safe.bareRepository` alone is causal.

## Acceptance criteria

All deterministic and verifiable in a single run — no waiting for a recurrence.

1. `env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<file setting safe.bareRepository=explicit> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 pytest
   tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py` exits 0 with 17 passed. (Today:
   5 failed, 12 passed.)
2. The same file still passes under default git config (17 passed), and the full
   `tests/interfaces/lifecycle` run still passes.
3. A regression oracle fails deterministically if the `git -C <bare-repo>` construct is reintroduced
   anywhere under `tests/`. Demonstrate by temporarily reverting one call site, observing the guard
   go RED, then restoring it.
4. The guard's coverage is **not** a hand-maintained file allowlist. If it remains one, then adding a
   new bare-fixture test without registering it must fail. Deriving the covered set from the tree is
   preferred — the hardcoded `_FIXTURE_NODES` list is precisely what let this recurrence through.

Note on the fix shape: `_git` is also called on **non-bare** worktrees (`tracker`, `writer`,
`tmp_path` for `init`/`clone`), so a blanket `-C` -> `--git-dir` swap is wrong. Only the five
bare-remote sites need the explicit form — e.g. a sibling `_git_bare(remote, ...)` helper.
fields.title: Bare-repo test fixtures regress: git -C <bare> in test_atomic_completion_close.py fails under safe.bareRepository=explicit (guard's hardcoded allowlist missed it)
